Pace, ratings and the four factors

Source: R/metrics.R
four_factors.Rd

Takes one row per team (season totals or single games) with the team's counting stats and the opponent's counting stats prefixed by o_ (o_p2a, o_tov, ...), and returns possessions, pace, offensive / defensive / net rating and Dean Oliver's four factors for offence and defence. Rows are kept, so you can pass grouped game data and summarise first, or pass totals directly.

Usage

four_factors(data, ft_coef = 0.44, min_is_team = TRUE, per = NULL)

Arguments

data

A data frame.

ft_coef

Passed to possessions().

min_is_team

Is min the sum of player minutes (240 per NBA game)?

per

Minutes the pace refers to (48 NBA, 40 FIBA).

Value

data with added columns poss, o_poss, pace, ortg, drtg, net_rtg, efg, tov_pct, orb_pct, ft_rate, o_efg, o_tov_pct, drb_pct, o_ft_rate.

Details

Columns needed: pts p2m p2a p3m p3a ftm fta orb drb tov and the same with o_. Optional min (team minutes, i.e. 5 x game minutes, or game minutes when min_is_team = FALSE) enables pace.

Examples

ff <- four_factors(team_seasons)
head(ff[, c("team", "league", "ortg", "drtg", "efg", "tov_pct")])
#> # A tibble: 6 × 6
#>   team  league      ortg  drtg   efg tov_pct
#>   <chr> <chr>      <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>   <dbl>
#> 1 ASV   EuroLeague  110.  115. 0.543   0.179
#> 2 BAR   EuroLeague  117.  112. 0.580   0.151
#> 3 BAS   EuroLeague  113.  114. 0.534   0.154
#> 4 BER   EuroLeague  102.  119. 0.512   0.189
#> 5 IST   EuroLeague  119.  112. 0.587   0.160
#> 6 MAD   EuroLeague  112.  109. 0.554   0.168
